filmhouse.title: Look Back
filmhouse.description: In a quiet town, Fujino is a confident elementary school student whose clever four-panel manga strips earn her idolization from her peers. Her artistic ego is shaken when the school paper begins publishing the astonishingly detailed artwork of Kyomoto, a reclusive classmate who refuses to leave her room. What begins as bitter jealousy transforms into a life-changing friendship when the two young creators join forces, forging an intense creative bond that carries them through the triumphs, heartbreaks, and haunting tragedies of growing into adulthood. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda (Shoplifters, Monster) and adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto’s (Chainsaw Man) one-shot manga of the same name, this acclaimed live-action drama premiered at the Venice International Film Festival. Shot on tactile 35mm film, Kore-eda’s sensitive adaptation pairs nuanced performances with a deeply moving exploration of artistic creation, grief, and the quiet human connections that forever shape our lives. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity.

filmhouse.title: The Violinist
filmhouse.description: Set across the shifting landscape of colonial Singapore and wartime Malaya, two musically gifted childhood friends—Fei and Kai—are bound together by their shared devotion to the violin. When the brutal onset of World War II and the Japanese Occupation tears them apart, Fei embarks on a decades-long journey across a changing Southeast Asia, holding onto memory, resilience, and the power of music as she searches for her lost friend. A landmark achievement for local cinema, co-directors Ervin Han and Raúl García’s hand-drawn feature made history by winning the prestigious Cristal Award for Best Feature at the Annecy International Animation Film Festival, alongside the SACEM Award for Best Original Soundtrack. Blending meticulous traditional craft with an evocative score by Ricky Ho, the film transforms regional history into a deeply human, universally resonant story that demands to be experienced on the big screen Director Q&A, Sunday 4 Oct Join us for an in-person Q&A with Co-Director Ervin Han , alongside Art Director and Storyboard Artist Ong Ruwei , Character Designer Sakura Wong and Animation Supervisor Wendy Li . In English with English and Mandarin subtitles. Rated PG for Some Violence

filmhouse.title: Wildwood
filmhouse.description: When her baby brother Mac is whisked away into an impenetrable, uncharted forest by a murder of crows, young Prue and her classmate Curtis ventures on a rescue mission. They stumble into a hidden realm where talking animals, mystical creatures, and warring factions vie for control. Drawn into an impending war orchestrated by the vengeful Countess Alexandra, Prue and Curtis must navigate treacherous alliances to save Mac and preserve the fragile balance of the magical wood. Directed by Travis Knight and produced by Laika(Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings), this epic stop-motion fantasy adapts Colin Meloy’s beloved novel into the animation studio’s most ambitious feature to date. Featuring the voices of Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, and Angela Bassett, the film blends tactile, hand-crafted puppet craft with sprawling scale, offering a thrilling and breathtaking coming-of-age adventure. In English Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: Fjord
filmhouse.description: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it. Winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, Fjord marks another masterclass in moral ambiguity from director Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, R.M.N.). Anchored by magnetic, career-defining performances from Stan and Reinsve, the film dissects the terrifying machinery of state intervention with surgical narrative precision. Framed in stark long-take cinematography that captures the icy, claustrophobic grandeur of its Scandinavian setting, Fjord is an explosive, thought-provoking drama bound to spark debate. In Romanian and Norwegian with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self-harm.

filmhouse.title: Godzilla Minus Zero
filmhouse.description: An allegory to nuclear weapons and unchecked military power, an insanely fun kaiju spectacle, or an adorable chonky boi that just wants to vibe, you decide what Godzilla and its legendary film franchise mean to you! War reduced Japan to zero, and Godzilla plunged it into minus. Two years have passed since then, and the country has faced agonizing struggles to achieve recovery and finally reclaim its daily life. Just as humanity managed to cling to a hard-won peace, a new threat strikes, crushing hope in an instant. There is no third time. Everything ends here. In Japanese with English and Chinese subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: In 19th-century Qing Dynasty China, renowned swordsman Li Mu Bai (Chow Yun Fat) decides to retire from his life of violence, entrusting his legendary 400-year-old sword, the Green Destiny, to his unspoken love, Yu Shu Lien(Michelle Yeoh). When the blade is stolen, suspicion falls on Jen Yu(Zhang Ziyi), a rebellious young noblewoman desperate to escape an arranged marriage. As Shu Lien and Mu Bai pursue the thief across breathtaking landscapes, they uncover a web of dark secrets and hidden identities. Directed by Ang Lee, this international cinematic phenomenon made history by winning four Academy Awards, including Best Foreign Language Film. Renowned for Yuen Wo-ping’s gravity-defying action choreography and Tan Dun’s iconic cello score, the film elevates traditional wuxia into a deeply romantic, tragic, and visually staggering masterpiece of passion and restraint. In Mandarin with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Intimate Scenes. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society

filmhouse.title: The Blade (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: In a lawless and brutal country dominated by ruthless bandit clans, Ding On works as a blacksmith’s apprentice in a remote sword factory. When he discovers the truth about his father's murder, Ding On sets off on a quest for revenge after bandit leader Fei Lung. In pursuit of vengeance, Ding On narrowly escapes an ambush, but loses his right arm in the process. Finding a half-burnt martial arts manual, he strengthens his resolve, forging a broken blade and adapting his fighting style to attain his retribution. Directed by Tsui Hark, this ferocious reimagining of Chang Cheh’s 1967 wuxia classic One-Armed Swordsman is a force of visual chaos and raw aggression. Driven by wild, immersive camerawork, and a gritty atmosphere, the film remains a visceral, influential cult classic. In Cantonese with English subtitles. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society Rated NC16 for Violence. TW: Contains depictions of animal abuse.

filmhouse.title: Hereditary
filmhouse.description: Following the death of her secretive mother, miniature artist Annie Graham attempts to navigate her family's complex grief while maintaining a semblance of order in her secluded home. As disturbing, unexplainable events begin to target her children, the family plunges into a nightmare of escalating trauma, revealing sinister secrets about their ancestry. Directed by Ari Aster in his astonishing feature debut, this modern horror masterpiece captivated audiences and critics alike, earning Toni Collette widespread acclaim for her staggering central performance. Blending agonizing familial drama with relentless, visceral dread, the film crafts a haunting exploration of inherited trauma and inescapable fate. In English with Mandarin subtitles. Rated M18 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self harm, animal cruelty and graphic scenes.

filmhouse.title: Fatherland
filmhouse.description: FATHERLAND centres on the relationship between the Nobel Prize-winning writer Thomas Mann and his daughter Erika, actress, writer and rally driver. In the summer of 1949, at the height of the Cold War, father and daughter embark on a challenging and emotional road trip in a black Buick taking them across a Germany in ruins – from US dominated Frankfurt to Soviet controlled Weimar. Returning home after sixteen years of exile in the US, Thomas Mann has to face not only a divided fatherland, but also deep fracture within his own family. In German with English subitltes . Rating NC16. Some Mature Content Co-presented by Goethe-Institut Singapore, Embassy of Italy in Singapore & Embassy of the Republic of Poland in Singapore TW: Contains scenes with flashing lights, photosentive audience is advised.

filmhouse.title: A Touch of Zen (4K Restoration)
filmhouse.description: In a quiet provincial town during the Ming Dynasty, Gu Sheng Zhai is a painter and scholar living with his mother near an abandoned estate. Fleeing from Government Officials who murdered her family after her father uncovers corruption, Noblewoman Yang Hui Zhen meets Sheng Zhai. The two convert the abandoned estate into a lethal trap, triggering an epic confrontation that escalates into a transcendental battle. Directed by King Hu, this landmark epic was the first Chinese language film to win a prize at the Cannes Film Festival, forever setting the gold standard for the wuxia genre. Featuring groundbreaking bamboo-forest action sequences and stunning cinematography, the film transforms a story of political vengeance into a grand masterpiece. In Mandarin with English subtitles. Rated PG13 for Some Violence. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society

filmhouse.title: La La Land (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Mia, an aspiring actress, serves lattes to movie stars in between auditions and Sebastian, a jazz musician, scrapes by playing cocktail party gigs in dingy bars, but as success mounts they are faced with decisions that begin to fray the fragile fabric of their love affair, and the dreams they worked so hard to maintain in each other threaten to rip them apart. In English with Mandarin Subtitles Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Language

filmhouse.title: Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea
filmhouse.description: One day, the red fish girl Ponyo hops on a jellyfish and leaves home, but gets her head stuck in a jam jar. Five-year-old Sosuke, who lives in a house on top of a cliff, finds Ponyo washed up on the shore and extracts her from the jar. They take a liking to each other, but Ponyo’s father Fujimoto forces her back into the sea. However, Ponyo wants to become human and live with Sosuke, so she enlists the help of her little sisters to steal her father’s magic, in an attempt to return to the world of humans. Conceived, Written, & Directed by Hayao Miyazaki In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated G.

filmhouse.title: All We Imagine as Light
filmhouse.description: In Mumbai, Prabha, a dedicated head nurse, buries her anxieties in her work while awaiting word from her estranged husband living abroad. Her younger, free-spirited roommate Anu struggles to find a private space in the bustling city to share with her secret Muslim lover. When the two women embark on a road trip to a coastal beach town alongside a retiring coworker, the change of setting offers them a space where their repressed desires, unspoken hopes, and bonds of sisterhood surfaces. Celebrated for its profound empathy, the Cannes Film Festival 2024 Grand Prix Winner offers a poetic, tender, and deeply moving portrait of female friendship, urban isolation, and the quiet search for freedom. In Malayalam, Hindi and Marathi with English subtitles . Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: Kokuho
filmhouse.description: Following its phenomenal success in Japan, critically acclaimed film Kokuho is enjoying a re-release in Singapore with limited screenings! Directed by acclaimed filmmaker Lee Sang-il and adapted from Shuichi Yoshida's bestselling novel of the same name, Kokuho stars Ryo Yoshizawa and Ryusei Yokohama alongside an impressive ensemble cast including Ken Watanabe. Set in the fascinating world of Kabuki, Japan's centuries-old traditional performing art, Kokuho tells the story of two young men from very different backgrounds whose lives become intertwined through their pursuit perfecting their craft. More than just a story about performance, Kokuho is a powerful portrait of ambition, identity and the price of dedicating one's life to art. Recognised by UNESCO as an Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, Kabuki is celebrated for its rich traditions, elaborate costumes and stylised performances. One of its most iconic features is “onnagata”, the art of male actors portraying female roles with extraordinary precision, grace and emotional depth. Since its release, Kokuho has become the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film in history. Domestic and global popularity of the film has also rekindled public interest in kabuki. The film dominated the 49th Japan Academy Film Prize, taking home ten awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Actor. Its exceptional Kabuki-inspired hair and makeup artistry also earned a nomination for Best Makeup and Hairstyling at the 98th Academy Awards, bringing the beauty of Japanese traditional culture to the global stage. In Japanese with English and Mandarin dual subtitles. Rated M18 for Sexual Scenes.

filmhouse.title: What We Do in the Shadows
filmhouse.description: In modern-day Wellington, New Zealand, a group of centuries-old vampires share a suburban flat and struggle with the mundane realities of modren domestic life. When a camera crew documents their daily routines, the arrival of a newly turned vampire and his human software-engineer friend introduces the ancient flatmates to contemporary culture, forcing them to adapt to the 21st century. Driven by razor-sharp improvisation, deadpan comedy, and inventive visual gags, this Taika Waititi classic offers a brilliant, endearing subversion of classic creature-feature tropes, earning its status as a cult classic. In English. Rated NC16 for Some Violence and Nudity.

filmhouse.title: Perfect Days
filmhouse.description: Hirayama works as a cleaner of public toilets in Tokyo, leading a quiet, contentment-driven life structured around classic rock cassettes, secondhand books, and photographing the light filtering through urban trees. As small, unexpected encounters break his daily routine, quiet details of his past gradually come to light. Directed by Wim Wenders, this Oscar nominee for Best International Feature earned Kōji Yakusho the Best Actor prize at the Cannes Film Festival. Celebrating the dignity of labor and the art of mindfulness, the film offers a warm, contemplative, and visually striking observation of contemporary Tokyo. In Japanese with English subitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity

filmhouse.description: In a quiet town, Fujino is a confident elementary school student whose clever four-panel manga strips earn her idolization from her peers. Her artistic ego is shaken when the school paper begins publishing the astonishingly detailed artwork of Kyomoto, a reclusive classmate who refuses to leave her room. What begins as bitter jealousy transforms into a life-changing friendship when the two young creators join forces, forging an intense creative bond that carries them through the triumphs, heartbreaks, and haunting tragedies of growing into adulthood. Directed by Hirokazu Kore-eda (Shoplifters, Monster) and adapted from Tatsuki Fujimoto’s (Chainsaw Man) one-shot manga of the same name, this acclaimed live-action drama premiered at the Venice International Film Festival. Shot on tactile 35mm film, Kore-eda’s sensitive adaptation pairs nuanced performances with a deeply moving exploration of artistic creation, grief, and the quiet human connections that forever shape our lives. In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated PG for Brief Nudity.

filmhouse.title: Wildwood
filmhouse.description: When her baby brother Mac is whisked away into an impenetrable, uncharted forest by a murder of crows, young Prue and her classmate Curtis ventures on a rescue mission. They stumble into a hidden realm where talking animals, mystical creatures, and warring factions vie for control. Drawn into an impending war orchestrated by the vengeful Countess Alexandra, Prue and Curtis must navigate treacherous alliances to save Mac and preserve the fragile balance of the magical wood. Directed by Travis Knight and produced by Laika(Coraline, Kubo and the Two Strings), this epic stop-motion fantasy adapts Colin Meloy’s beloved novel into the animation studio’s most ambitious feature to date. Featuring the voices of Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, and Angela Bassett, the film blends tactile, hand-crafted puppet craft with sprawling scale, offering a thrilling and breathtaking coming-of-age adventure. In English Rated PG13 for Some Violence.

filmhouse.title: Fjord
filmhouse.description: The Gheorghius, a devout Romanian Norwegian couple, resettle in a village set in a distant fjord where they become close to their neighbours, the Halbergs. Their children bond despite their different education. When adolescent Elia Gheorghiu shows up at school with some bruises on her body, the community asks itself if the traditional education that the Gheorghiu children get from their parents might have anything to do with it. Winner of the Palme d’Or at the Cannes Film Festival, Fjord marks another masterclass in moral ambiguity from director Cristian Mungiu (4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, R.M.N.). Anchored by magnetic, career-defining performances from Stan and Reinsve, the film dissects the terrifying machinery of state intervention with surgical narrative precision. Framed in stark long-take cinematography that captures the icy, claustrophobic grandeur of its Scandinavian setting, Fjord is an explosive, thought-provoking drama bound to spark debate. In Romanian and Norwegian with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Some Nudity. TW: Contains depictions of self-harm.

filmhouse.title: Moonlight (10th Anniversary)
filmhouse.description: Framed across three pivotal eras of his life, Chiron navigates the harsh realities of growing up in a tough neighborhood while struggling with his identity, sexuality, and a troubled home environment. Guided by the tender mentorship of a local drug dealer and a deep, enduring connection with a childhood friend, Chiron gradually leanrs to protect himself from the world as he grows into adulthood. Directed by Barry Jenkins, this groundbreaking drama won three Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Supporting Actor for Mahershala Ali. Celebrated for James Laxton’s luminous cinematography and Nicholas Britell’s evocative score, the film stands as a transcendent, deeply lyrical portrait of intimacy, vulnerability, and self-discovery. Newly restored in 4K and with an exclusive conversation with director Barry Jenkins, featuring Oscar Nominated composer Nicholas Britell and Oscar winner Mahershala Ali, to follow the feature. In English. Rated M18 for Some Homosexual Content.

filmhouse.title: This Is Spinal Tap
filmhouse.description: Accompanied by documentarian Marty DiBergi, legendary British heavy metal outfit Spinal Tap embarks on a disastrous 1982 U.S. tour to promote their new album, Smell the Glove. As the band faces plummeting ticket sales, canceled gig venues, undersized Stonehenge stage props, and a revolving door of spontaneously combusting drummers, the unraveling dynamics between co-founders Nigel Tufnel and David St. Hubbins threaten to destroy the group once and for all. Directed by Rob Reiner and co-created alongside stars Christopher Guest, Michael McKean, and Harry Shearer, this groundbreaking mockumentary defined a genre and was preserved in the National Film Registry. Driven by brilliant, razor-sharp improvisation and parody rock anthems that turn the volume up to eleven, the film delivers a timeless, hilarious satire on rock 'n' roll megalomania and artistic delusions. In English . Rated PG13 for Some Coarse Langauge and Drug References. Metal Karaoke! Wednesday, 11 Nov, 9.30pm Filmhouse Foyer Accompanying the exclusive screening of This Is Spinal Tap, the Foyer goes one louder this Metal Day (11.11.26) From Thrash to Nu, selectors @kkkidggg of @eatmepoptart and thebryanstate of @emonightsg reveal a musical side to them not commonly seen behind the decks, expect unhinged headbangable sets in celebration of Metal through the ages. After which a midweek catharsis awaits as METAL KARAOKE begins and the floor is dedicated to you and your crew. All your favourite tunes are on standby and are yours to sing/scream/squeal. Drinks are available at the bar Entry is free, and all are welcome

filmhouse.title: The House on the Moon
filmhouse.description: In a fantastical realm where the sun is dying, the legendary archer Ho Yi vanishes on a desperate quest to restore its light. Consumed by worry, his lover and fairy maiden Chang Er, adventures to the moon's unexplored dark side to find him. Crossing paths with an earthbound bandit whose vessel crash-lands in her domain, the mismatched pair must navigate dreamlike topographies, ancient mythologies, and their conflicting desires in a race against cosmic darkness. Directed by Nelson Yeo, this spellbinding Singaporean-Taiwanese co-production premiered in competition at Locarno Film Festival 2026. Blending folklore, surrealist imagery, and poignant intimacy, the film offers a visually poetic and hauntingly romantic reimagining of the classic Eastern mythology. *Join us on November 12 for the opening screening and an in-person Q&A with Director Nelson Yeo, and lead actress Shi-An Lim In Mandarin with English subtitles. Rated NC16 for Sexual Scene and Some Mature Content. The Way Of The Sword: Wuxia Masters is co-presented by Filmhouse and Momo Film Co, and supported by Singapore Film Society

filmhouse.title: Ponyo on the Cliff by the Sea
filmhouse.description: One day, the red fish girl Ponyo hops on a jellyfish and leaves home, but gets her head stuck in a jam jar. Five-year-old Sosuke, who lives in a house on top of a cliff, finds Ponyo washed up on the shore and extracts her from the jar. They take a liking to each other, but Ponyo’s father Fujimoto forces her back into the sea. However, Ponyo wants to become human and live with Sosuke, so she enlists the help of her little sisters to steal her father’s magic, in an attempt to return to the world of humans. Conceived, Written, & Directed by Hayao Miyazaki In Japanese with English subtitles. Rated G.

upcoming.title: Ebenezer
upcoming.description: This November, Johnny Depp is Ebenezer Scrooge. The name you know, the story you don’t. EBENEZER follows a miserly businessman who is forced through visions of the past, present, and future during a supernatural journey toward a chance at redemption.

upcoming.title: How To Rob A Bank
upcoming.description: Nicholas Hoult and Pete Davidson are part of a group of bank robbers who share their heists on social media in this tongue-in-cheek thriller from the director of Bullet Train.

upcoming.title: THE BEAST
upcoming.description: When a militia of unidentified hostiles coordinates a coup against the U.S., the president uncovers the extent of The Beast's highly classified offensive capabilities in order to save his life and America.

upcoming.title: Ah Girl [M]
upcoming.description: Seven-year-old Ah Girl (Ong Xuan Jing) is growing up fast in 1990s Singapore. Her parents are separated and she lives with lazy, charming Pa (James Seah), naughty sister Ah Tian (Sydney Wong) and grumpy Ah Ma (Doreen Toh), while craving affection from aloof Mummy (Carrie Wong). Despite the chaos and conflict of her broken family, Ah Girl finds time to collect spiders, have a crush, and sell bubblegum, but can she stay true to herself when the adults threaten to make things worse?

upcoming.title: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping
upcoming.description: From acclaimed director Francis Lawrence, THE HUNGER GAMES: SUNRISE ON THE REAPING follows sixteen-year-old Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) from District 12, beginning on the morning of the reaping for the 50th Annual Hunger Games, also known as the Second Quarter Quell, the biggest Games yet with twice as many tributes.

upcoming.title: George Michael - The Faith Tour
upcoming.description: George Michael was one of the most influential stars of his generation; his voice and songwriting defined an era. Assembled from rediscovered, previously unseen and unheard 35mm footage of his 1988 performance at the Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy, this new concert film captures George at the height of his creative power during the record-breaking Faith Tour. Expertly restored and remastered, the film transforms a defining cultural moment into a spectacular cinema experience. An original short film by Mary McCartney opens the feature, using newly discovered audio and imagery from 1986–1988 – the Faith era – creating a rare and intimate ‘time capsule’, offering a vivid insight into George’s mindset at this pivotal moment in his life.

upcoming.title: OM Chapter 1: Udhiram - The Blood Wood [TAM]
upcoming.description: Follows a man who saves 20 Tamil woodcutters arrested by police in a forest in Tiruvannamalai.

upcoming.title: Disney's Hexed
upcoming.description: In Walt Disney Animation Studios' all-new magical coming-of-age saga, “Hexed,” an impulsive and unconventional teenage girl named Billie (voice of Hailee Steinfeld) discovers secret magical abilities which, once unleashed, hurtle her into a spectacle-filled journey out of suburbia and into a vast witch realm called Hexe. Forced to team up with her cautious mother, Alice (voice of Rashida Jones), they uncover family mysteries that could change the world of witches forever.

upcoming.title: Focker In-Law
upcoming.description: The circle of trust just got bigger. This November, comedy icon and Emmy winner Ben Stiller and two-time Oscar winner Robert De Niro reunite, joined by Grammy winner and Oscar nominee Ariana Grande, in Focker-In-Law, a new chapter in the blockbuster Meet the Parents franchise.

upcoming.title: Winter Of The Crow (POLISH)
upcoming.description: A British professor witnesses a student's murder by secret police in 1981 Warsaw under martial law. She becomes a target while running through the city's streets, eventually forced to stop and take a stand.

upcoming.title: You Can See Everything
upcoming.description:
Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew
to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigmatic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey
into the abyss. From boundary-pushing directors Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim comes YOU CAN SEE EVERYTHING.

upcoming.title: Bitter Christmas (SPANISH)
upcoming.description: In 2004, an ad director faces a turbulent Christmas weekend. In 2026, a filmmaker turns her story into a screenplay, blurring the lines between reality, fiction, and the people closest to him.

upcoming.title: Dune
upcoming.description: This is an IMAX reissue of Dune (2021), bringing the epic Part One back to the big screen. Watch it again or experience it for the first time before Dune: Part Two is released on February 29, 2024.

upcoming.title: I Play Rocky
upcoming.description: The film is an electrifying true story about an unknown actor with an unshakable belief that he wasn’t just meant to write Rocky—he was meant to be Rocky Balboa. Told “no” at every turn, Sylvester Stallone bets everything on himself, holding the line on playing the lead against seemingly impossible odds. The result is the ultimate underdog story behind the ultimate underdog movie.

upcoming.title: Violent Night 2
upcoming.description: When Santa forgets the true meaning of Christmas, he finds himself in the heart of a lively mall community in desperate need of his help. Sapped of his magic, he'll need another way to take on the goons threatening the mall, and time is running out. Santa has to rediscover his faith in goodness and call in some last-minute reinforcements from the one person no baddie wants to tangle with: Mrs. Claus (Emmy and Golden Globe nominee Kristen Bell).

upcoming.title: Funny Face (1957)
upcoming.description: Jo Stockton is a bookshop clerk who might just have what it takes to be a modelling sensation. After inadvertently being discovered by fashion photographer Dick Avery, she is offered the chance to become the next big thing. Initially sceptical of the model lifestyle, Jo only agrees when a trip to Paris and the opportunity to meet her intellectual hero are thrown into the bargain.

upcoming.title: Dune: Part Three
upcoming.description: Dune: Part Three is based on the novel Dune Messiah by Frank Herbert and delivers the epic conclusion to Villeneuve’s trilogy.

upcoming.title: Marvel Studios' Avengers: Doomsday
upcoming.description: Heroes from three different worlds must unite when they're thrust together to confront a catastrophic danger that could destroy everything they know.

upcoming.title: Jumanji: Open World
upcoming.description: The players have escaped the ever-changing jungles of Jumanji, but this time the game breaks free of its console, unleashing chaos into our world.

upcoming.title: A Talent For Murder
upcoming.description: A mysterious young man from a New York publisher is sent to Switzerland to persuade the renowned writer Patricia Highsmith to write one final installment of the Ripley anthology.

upcoming.title: The Angry Birds Movie 3
upcoming.description: Red faces his greatest challenge yet, which is being a dad - and also saving the world.

upcoming.title: Ice Age: Boiling Point
upcoming.description: Manny, Sid, Diego, Ellie, Buck, and the rest of the herd blast out of a volcano and embark on a dinosaur-and-lava-filled adventure through uncharted parts of the treacherous Lost World.

upcoming.title: Disney and Pixar's Gatto
upcoming.description: In Disney and Pixar's “Gatto,” the scrappy black cat Nero begins to question whether he’s lived the right lives after years of maneuvering the canal-ridden, superstitious city of Venice, Italy. Indebted to Rocco, the ruthless local feline mob boss, Nero finds himself in a quandary and is forced to forge a truly unexpected friendship that may finally lead him to his purpose - unless Venice gets the better of him first.
